cards.title: THE HALL CLOSET
cards.tagline: FIVE SHELVES OF EVERYTHING WITH NOWHERE ELSE TO GO. START WITH THE ONE YOU CAN'T SEE THE BACK OF.
cards.objective: The hall closet is the darkest and deepest storage in the house, and the only one nobody owns. This card is the map and the order.
cards.start_here: HCZ-001 Linen Shelf Zone. Empty one shelf onto the hallway floor before you touch anything else. A closet this deep cannot be sorted in place; you have to see the back wall to know what you own.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the five ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your closet. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do HCA-011 The Full Shelf Weight And Reach Safety Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers every shelf's height, the stool, and every loaded bracket.

cards.title: LINEN SHELF ZONE
cards.tagline: THREE SETS PER BED. ONE PILLOWCASE EACH. THE COUNT ON THE SHELF.
cards.objective: Holds the sheets, towels, and blankets the beds in this house actually rotate through.

Queen and king sets stored low, guest blankets on top
No loose, unmatched sheet lying outside a bundle

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Pulling a towel from the bottom of a chest-high stack brings the whole pile down onto your face and the hallway floor.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Damp-weight blankets and a full shelf of folded cotton are heavier than they look; check the shelf brackets are screwed into studs, not just into plasterboard.

the_call.title: The good set you never put on a bed
the_call.text: There is a sheet set here that is too nice to use and too nice to give away, so it has sat at the front of the shelf for years while you sleep on the worn ones. Settle it with a date: put it on a bed this month, or accept that it is a keepsake rather than a linen. Keepsakes can live in a memory box. They cannot live on the shelf you reach into every week.

Broom, mop, and duster hanging handle-down from wall clips with the heads clear of the floor. The closet door swinging fully open without touching anything.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Unclipped handles slide down the wall and drop across the doorway or onto whoever opens the door.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: A damp mop head or a wet bucket stored against a vacuum cord in a closed closet is the one combination to refuse; check the cord for cracked insulation near the plug while you have it out.

the_call.title: The vacuum you keep meaning to fix
the_call.text: It has a split hose or a dead brush roll, and it sits here because throwing out a machine that mostly works feels wasteful. Give it a repair date written on masking tape stuck to the body. If that date passes and you have not ordered the part, you have your answer: the repair was never going to happen, and the broken machine has been standing where the working one needs to stand. Recycle it and keep the one that runs.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Bleach stored beside an ammonia glass cleaner, and any product in an unlabeled bottle at a height a child can reach from the hallway floor.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: Aerosol tins and solvent-based sprays sitting against a closet wall that backs onto a boiler or a hot water pipe; move them to the coolest shelf.

the_call.title: Eleven bottles, each a third full
the_call.text: You buy a new one because you cannot see what is left in the old one, and the shelf now carries four glass cleaners, three floor sprays, and a scatter of part-used others. The rule that settles it: one open bottle per job. Pour identical products together, and for the rest, accept that finishing a half bottle down the drain costs you a little while keeping it costs you the shelf you need. You did not save money by keeping them. You paid twice and stored the evidence.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Button cells and loose AAAs rolling to the closet floor where a small child finds them at eye level.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A shrink-wrapped bulk pack of paper towel stored above head height slides free the moment you tug the corner of it.

the_call.title: The offer that made you buy twelve
the_call.text: Bulk buying feels thrifty right up to the point where a warehouse pack blocks the shelf and you buy more anyway because you cannot see past it. Set your maximum as the number that fits inside the bin without stacking above the rim, then hold it: if a deal will not fit the bin, the deal is not for you. And date each pack with a marker as it arrives, pulling the oldest first. Undated bulk is where the saving quietly expires.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Reaching for a top-shelf bin while balanced on a hallway chair, with a lid you cannot see over hiding the step down.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A bin of decorations lifted down overhead shifts its weight halfway and lands on your foot or on whoever is holding the door.

the_call.title: The bin you have moved three times without opening
the_call.text: It has survived a house move and two closet reshuffles, and you still cannot say what is in it. That is the decision you have been avoiding, and the avoidance is itself the answer. Open it on the floor today. For each thing inside, name the specific occasion in the next twelve months when you will use it: a birthday, a holiday, a trip already booked. Anything you cannot name an occasion for does not get the lid back on, because a sealed bin of unknowns is not storage, it is a decision you agreed to keep paying for.

cards.objective: The thing has no single defined destination, so it lands wherever the hand opens.

cards.objective: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask someone who does not live here to name what looks out of place. If they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, this is the cause.

cards.title: UNFOLD EVERY SET AND CHECK IT'S WHOLE
cards.objective: Pull every sheet set off the shelf, unfold each one fully, and check it is complete and still fits a bed in this house.
cards.why_it_matters: A set that's missing its match or gone slack at the elastic is impossible to use in the moment you actually reach for it.
steps: Pull every sheet set off the shelf, unfold each one fully, and check it's complete and still fits a bed you still own: the flat sheet with no fitted match, the elastic that's gone slack, and anything that smells sour after drying all leave today.
Set aside anything unopened and genuinely still useful to give away rather than binning it.
Refold what stays to one width and group by bed size.
cards.victory_condition: Every remaining set is a complete, matching set that fits a real bed, and nothing waits folded that failed the check.

art.subject: a hallway closet shelf mid-clear with unfolded sheet sets laid out on the floor, one incomplete set set apart from the rest
must_show: Every remaining set is a complete, matching set that fits a real bed, and nothing waits folded that failed the check.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: BUNDLE EACH SET AND LABEL THE SHELF EDGE
cards.objective: Fold each set to one uniform footprint, bundle it inside its own pillowcase, and write the bed size and count on the shelf edge.
cards.why_it_matters: A shelf label that only names the size and not the count still leaves a laundry-day guess.
steps: Fold each set to one uniform footprint and bundle it inside its own pillowcase so a bed change is one grab, not four.
Group bundles by bed size: queen and king low, everyday towels at chest height, guest blankets on top.
Write the size and count on the shelf edge underneath, not just the name.
cards.victory_condition: Every bed's sets are bundled inside their own pillowcases, and the shelf edge names both the size and the count.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand writing a bed size and a count onto a shelf-edge label beneath a shelf of pillowcase-bundled sheet sets
must_show: Every bed's sets are bundled inside their own pillowcases, and the shelf edge names both the size and the count.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: STAND UP EVERY TOOL AND CHECK THE WORKING END
cards.objective: Stand every handle up and look at the working end, removing anything that no longer does its job.
cards.why_it_matters: A broom that pushes dust instead of gathering it, or a spare vacuum kept for parts never harvested, is taking up the spot a working tool needs.
steps: Stand every handle up and look at the working end: brooms with splayed bristles that push dust rather than gather it, a mop head that no longer twists off its plate, and the old vacuum you keep for parts you've never once harvested all go out this week.
Recycle what can be recycled, and clear the floor space they were taking.
cards.victory_condition: Only tools that actually do their job stand in this closet, and nothing broken is waiting on a repair that was never going to happen.

art.subject: a row of cleaning tools standing upright in a hallway closet, one broom with splayed bristles set apart to be discarded
must_show: Only tools that actually do their job stand in this closet, and nothing broken is waiting on a repair that was never going to happen.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: FIT THE RAIL AND TAPE THE VACUUM'S OUTLINE
cards.objective: Fit a rail so each tool hangs with its head clear of the floor, and tape a floor outline for the vacuum with its attachments bagged on the handle.
cards.why_it_matters: A mop head left standing on the floor bends over and re-soils what you just cleaned, and an unclipped handle is what slides down across the doorway.
inputs: a small zip bag for attachments
steps: Fit a rail and hang each tool so bristles and mop heads swing free of the floor.
Tape an outline for the vacuum's footprint on the closet floor.
Zip the crevice tools and brush heads into one bag clipped to the vacuum's handle.
cards.victory_condition: Handles hang from the rail with heads clear of the floor, the vacuum parks inside its taped outline, and the attachment bag rides on its handle.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a wall-mounted rail in a hallway closet holding a broom, mop and duster hanging handle-down, a taped floor outline visible below with a vacuum parked inside it
must_show: Handles hang from the rail with heads clear of the floor, the vacuum parks inside its taped outline, and the attachment bag rides on its handle.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LINE UP EVERY BOTTLE AND CLEAR THE UNMARKED ONES
cards.objective: Line every bottle up on the hallway floor, and remove anything decanted into an unmarked spray bottle or bought for one old stain.
cards.why_it_matters: A bottle with no legible original label is a guess every time you reach for it, and pouring like into like is the only way to know what's actually here.
steps: Line every bottle up on the hallway floor. Anything decanted into an unmarked spray bottle is disposed of according to its own product's instructions, and the specialty cleaner bought for one old stain goes with it.
Pour only identical products together into one bottle.
Set the survivors back with every label facing out.
cards.victory_condition: Every bottle on the shelf carries its own legible original label, and only one open bottle of each job remains.

art.subject: cleaning bottles lined up on a hallway floor, one unmarked spray bottle set apart from a row of clearly labeled ones
must_show: Every bottle on the shelf carries its own legible original label, and only one open bottle of each job remains.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: BUILD ONE CADDY PER ROOM
cards.objective: Build a bathroom caddy and a kitchen caddy so the whole job for that room travels in one hand, and keep bleach and ammonia products on separate shelves.
cards.why_it_matters: Sending yourself back to this closet twice mid-clean is the walk this caddy exists to remove, and bleach beside ammonia is the one combination to refuse outright.
inputs: adhesive labels for the caddy ends
steps: Build a bathroom caddy and a kitchen caddy, with gloves and cloths riding inside each one alongside the sprays.
Label each caddy's end with the room it serves.
Move bleach products and ammonia products onto separate shelves, out of a small child's reach or behind a latch.
cards.victory_condition: One caddy per room carries its own labeled sprays and cloths, and bleach and ammonia products sit on separate shelves.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: two labeled cleaning caddies standing ready in a hallway closet, one marked for the bathroom and one for the kitchen, bleach and ammonia products visible on separate shelves behind them
must_show: One caddy per room carries its own labeled sprays and cloths, and bleach and ammonia products sit on separate shelves.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: TAKE THE LOT OUT AND SORT BY SIZE
cards.objective: Take every battery, bulb, and paper pack out onto the hallway floor, removing anything you can't vouch for or can't lift safely alone.
cards.why_it_matters: A loose battery nobody can vouch for and a fitting you replaced months ago are both still costing this shelf space.
steps: Take the lot out. Loose batteries you cannot vouch for, bulbs for fittings you replaced when you went over to LED, and any bulk pack too big to lift down alone all leave now.
Sort surviving batteries upright in a shallow tray by size, and box bulbs together by fitting.
Set the heaviest remaining packs at waist height, not overhead.
cards.victory_condition: Every battery is sorted by size in its tray, every bulb is boxed by fitting, and nothing left on the shelf is too heavy or too high to lift down alone.

art.subject: batteries and bulbs spread out on a hallway floor being sorted into a shallow tray and a labeled bin, an oversized pack set apart to be moved
must_show: Every battery is sorted by size in its tray, every bulb is boxed by fitting, and nothing left on the shelf is too heavy or too high to lift down alone.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: WRITE A MINIMUM AND MAXIMUM ON EVERY BIN
cards.objective: Write a minimum and a maximum on the shelf edge in front of each bin, sized to what the bin can hold without stacking above its rim.
cards.why_it_matters: A number in your head is not a number anyone else can read, and an undated bulk pack is where a saving quietly expires.
steps: Set the maximum for each bin as the count that fits inside it without stacking above the rim.
Write both the minimum and maximum on the shelf edge in front of each bin.
Date every pack with a marker as it goes back, oldest at the front.
cards.victory_condition: Every bin carries a minimum and maximum on its shelf edge, and every pack behind it is dated with the oldest at the front.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand writing a minimum and maximum onto a shelf-edge label in front of a hallway closet bin, dated packs visible behind it
must_show: Every bin carries a minimum and maximum on its shelf edge, and every pack behind it is dated with the oldest at the front.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: OPEN EVERY LID ON THE FLOOR, IN DAYLIGHT
cards.objective: Take every lid off, on the floor, in daylight, and remove anything you can't name from memory.
cards.why_it_matters: A sealed bin of unknowns is not storage, it is a decision you agreed to keep paying for.
steps: Take every lid off, on the floor, in daylight. Decorations for a tree you no longer put up, a guest pillow gone flat and yellow, and any bin marked misc whose contents you cannot name without looking all go.
For each remaining item, name the specific occasion in the next twelve months when it will be used.
Anything with no named occasion does not get the lid back on.
cards.victory_condition: Every remaining bin holds one named occasion, and nothing sealed inside it is something you couldn't name from memory.

art.subject: storage bins opened on a hallway floor in daylight, their contents spread out for sorting, one bin marked misc set apart
must_show: Every remaining bin holds one named occasion, and nothing sealed inside it is something you couldn't name from memory.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LABEL EVERY BIN, DATE THE LID, MAP THE SHELF
cards.objective: Label each bin with its contents and the date it was last closed, photograph it packed, and tape a shelf map inside the door.
cards.why_it_matters: A photograph taped to the lid gives repacking a target instead of a guess, and a shelf map means someone else can find the guest bedding without unstacking the shelf.
steps: Label each bin with what's inside and the date it was last closed.
Photograph each bin packed and tape the picture to the lid.
Tape a simple shelf map inside the closet door showing which bin sits where.
cards.victory_condition: Every bin is labeled with contents and a closing date, carries a photo of itself packed, and the door holds a shelf map that matches the shelves.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a labeled storage bin with a photograph taped to its lid, a shelf map taped inside a hallway closet door visible behind it

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FULL SHELF WEIGHT AND REACH SAFETY WALK
cards.objective: Walk every shelf checking what's stored above head height, whether a stool lives in reach, and that the brackets holding the heaviest loads are sound.
cards.why_it_matters: A heavy bin overhead and a hallway chair standing in for a stool both hide until someone tests for them on purpose.
steps: Check every shelf for anything heavy stored above head height, and move it down to a lower shelf.
Confirm a real step stool lives near this closet, not a hallway chair standing in for one.
Check the shelf brackets are screwed into studs, not just into plasterboard, under the heaviest loads.
cards.victory_condition: Nothing heavy sits above head height, a real stool lives within reach, and every loaded bracket is anchored into a stud.

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE WEEKLY BEFORE-THE-LIST CHECK
cards.objective: Walk the paper, battery, and bulb bins reading what's low before the shopping list gets written, and name who is doing it this week.
cards.why_it_matters: Everybody takes the last roll and almost nobody mentions it, so this zone fails silently unless somebody is actually assigned to look.
steps: Walk the backstock bins and read each one against its written minimum before the list gets written.
Say out loud, or write down, whose turn it is to do this pass this week.
Add anything genuinely below its minimum to the list on the spot.
cards.victory_condition: The bins were read against their written minimums before this week's list was written, and one named person did it.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand writing an item onto a shopping list while standing in front of a hallway closet bin sitting below its own shelf-edge minimum

cards.title: THE SEASONAL MAXIMUM AND LABEL AUDIT
cards.objective: Once a season, check every written maximum and every bin label against what's actually on the shelves, correcting anything that has drifted.
cards.why_it_matters: A maximum or a label written once and never revisited stops meaning anything the first time a good deal or a quiet clear-out moves past it.
inputs: this season's receipts if you kept them
steps: Compare the count behind each bin against its written maximum, and note any line that has crept over.
Relabel any bin whose contents or closing date no longer match what's inside it.
Correct the shelf map inside the door if a bin has moved.
cards.victory_condition: Every bin sits at or under a maximum checked this season, and every label and the shelf map both match what's actually on the shelves.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand comparing a bin's count against a shelf-edge maximum label in a hallway closet, a shelf map taped inside the door beside it

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LINEN SHELF ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Three sets per bed, each nested in its own pillowcase, with the size and count written on the shelf edge.
cards.trigger: When you strip the beds on laundry day, the fresh set comes off this shelf and you read the count as you lift it.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Run a hand along the shelf's front lip and check for the grey dust line before it thickens onto the clean stack below it.
Wipe the shelf brackets and the underside of the board above with a dry cloth, catching the fluff that clings and drops onto the stack.
Shake out one folded sheet set and refold it to the same width as its neighbors, checking for a musty note as you go.

cards.title: CLEANING EQUIPMENT ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Handles hang from the rail with heads clear of the floor, the vacuum parks inside its outline, and nothing goes in wet.
cards.trigger: When the vacuum is switched off after a clean, it is wrapped, bagged, and back inside the tape before you sit down.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Empty the vacuum canister into the bin and wipe it out before it goes back inside the taped outline.
Comb the broom bristles clear of trapped hair and thread, letting nothing carry back onto the floor you just swept.
Run each cord through a folded cloth along its whole length as you coil it, lifting off the dust that collects in the loops.

must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: CLEANING SUPPLY ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: One caddy per room, one open bottle per job, original labels only, and bleach and ammonia kept apart.
cards.trigger: When the caddy is set back on the shelf after a clean, whatever ran out is written on the list in the same movement.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the crusted ring off the base of one bottle and clean the dried run down its neck before it goes back on the shelf.
Lift the shelf liner, rinse both faces, and lay it back flat so the next slow drip lands on something wipeable.
Wipe the inside of a caddy's divider walls and its handle where product residue gathers most.

art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: PAPER AND HOUSEHOLD BACKSTOCK STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Every bin carries a minimum and maximum on the shelf edge, stock is dated with a marker on arrival, and the oldest pack is pulled first.
cards.trigger: When you take the last roll or the last pack of bulbs out of a bin, the restock goes on the shopping list on that same trip to the closet.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Lift the battery tray out, wipe the bottom clean, and watch for a white crust before it dries back before the batteries return.
Press the underside of one paper pack stored against the outside wall to check for damp before it soaks through unnoticed.
Tip the paper dust and cardboard flecks from the bottom corners of the toilet-roll bin before it goes back on the shelf.

cards.title: SEASONAL AND GUEST ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Every bin is lidded, labeled with contents and the date it was last closed, photographed inside the lid, and stored clean and dry.
cards.trigger: When the guest bed is stripped after a visit, the bedding is washed and returned to its own bin before the closet door shuts.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Put your nose to the bottom of one open bin and check for the mustiness that means something went in damp.
Wipe the dust off the top of a bin lid before you set it aside, so none of it tips down into the open bin below.
Check the shelf map taped inside the closet door is still legible and still matches what's actually on each shelf.

art.subject: a hallway closet upper shelf holding lidded storage bins each labeled with contents and a closing date, a photograph taped to one lid, and a shelf map taped inside the closet door, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: THE MIDNIGHT SHEET CHANGE
cards.objective: A child is sick at midnight and the bed needs fresh sheets right now, no time to hunt.
cards.held_if: The right size set comes off the shelf in one bundle, no digging through mismatched pieces.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to unfold three sets to find one complete match, the check-and-bundle habit slipped. Draw HCA-001.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a hand pulling one bundled sheet set from a hallway closet shelf quickly at night
must_show: A child is sick at midnight and the bed needs fresh sheets right now, no time to hunt.
art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people's faces, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces and, where unavoidable, by hands and feet alone.

cards.title: THE SPILL THAT NEEDS EVERYTHING AT ONCE
cards.objective: Something spills across the kitchen floor and the mop, the bucket and gloves all have to come out together, right now.
cards.held_if: Every tool comes off the rail already working, with nothing missing from the bag on the handle.
cards.if_it_failed: If a tool was broken or an attachment was missing from the bag, the stand-up check or the rail habit slipped. Draw HCA-003.

cards.title: THE GUEST ARRIVING IN AN HOUR
cards.objective: Guests are due in an hour and the bathroom and kitchen both need a fast, real clean.
cards.held_if: Grabbing the bathroom caddy in one hand gets the whole job there without a second trip to this closet.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to come back for a bottle the caddy should have held, the one-caddy-per-room habit slipped. Draw HCA-006.

cards.title: THE POWER CUT THAT NEEDS A FLASHLIGHT NOW
cards.objective: The power goes out at night and the flashlight needs batteries that actually work, immediately.
cards.held_if: The right size battery is standing upright in its tray, sorted and easy to find in the dark.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to feel around for a loose battery you couldn't vouch for, the sort-by-size habit slipped. Draw HCA-007.

cards.title: THE OVERNIGHT GUEST WITH NO WARNING
cards.objective: Somebody needs the guest bed made up tonight, with no notice.
cards.held_if: The guest bedding is clean, in its own labeled bin, and the shelf map says exactly where to find it.
cards.if_it_failed: If the bedding had drifted onto the everyday shelf or the bin had no date, the wash-and-return habit slipped. Draw HCA-010.
